tools.name: call_tool
tools.title: Call any allowed tool
tools.description: Call a tool from any allowed pack by its full name (for example hub_find_low_stock) without it being listed. Arguments follow that tool's own input schema, which find_tools returns.

name.description: The tool's gateway name, e.g. hub_get_products or flow_list_flows.

tools.name: disable_packs
tools.title: List fewer packs
tools.description: Remove packs from tools/list for this connection to keep the list short. Tools stay reachable through call_tool.

tools.name: enable_packs
tools.title: List more packs
tools.description: Add packs to tools/list for this connection (remembered). Only allowed packs can be listed; the client refreshes its tool list.

tools.name: find_tools
tools.title: Find tools
tools.description: Search every allowed pack for tools by what you want to do ("low stock", "create a product", "deploy the app"). Returns matching tool names with their pack and whether they are listed. Call a match with call_tool, or enable_packs to list its pack.

query.description: Plain-language description of the task or the record type.

tools.name: flow_apply_blueprint_widgets
tools.title: Apply blueprint widgets into a flow
tools.description: COPY vetted blueprint widgets into a flow as real files — byte-exact, no transcription. Pass picks of { blueprintId, widgetId } (from list_blueprints / search_blueprints); the widget files land under src/widgets/<blueprint>/ with their command-frame plumbing intact, persisted as a restorable checkpoint + builder-chat note like write_flow_files. Returns a manifest (paths, export names, props, a ready-to-paste import block) — never the code. Compose your screens by importing the manifest paths; adapt an applied widget with a small write_flow_files edit, never a wholesale rewrite, and never re-type code from get_blueprint. A selfPersisting blueprint's copied code reads/writes its OWN custom tables by exact name: this tool PROVISIONS those tables into your organization automatically, possibly under org-scoped names (see `tables` in the result — the copied code already uses the final names) — never create them yourself and never create a lookalike. Tables owned by a platform extension are reported under `extensionTables` (with extensionIds when pinned): only installing that extension provides them (install_extension, with user consent). Secrets the code reads are reported under `secrets` — each missing key gets a fill-in request in the builder automatically; values never travel over MCP. Re-applying a pick restores the widget's vetted contents.

note.description: One-line summary of the change, shown in the builder chat.

hubToken.description: Optional organization JWT for the Final hub, used to provision the blueprint's custom tables when your organization has no stored hub credential.

tools.name: flow_apply_upstream_update
tools.title: Apply an upstream update to a clone
tools.description: Apply the update reviewed with get_upstream_update. Pass resolutions: exactly one entry per conflict — { path, contents } with the COMPLETE merged file, or { path, delete: true } when the file should not exist. Missing, unknown or ambiguous entries fail the whole call with nothing written (the plan is recomputed here, so re-review if the flow changed since). What it does, in order: saves the current files as a restorable "Before update" checkpoint, lands the merged tree (an open builder tab picks it up safely), records an "Update from upstream vX" checkpoint narrated in the builder chat, re-stamps the clone's update pointer so the next check compares against this release, provisions custom tables the update introduced (org-scoped names — the merged code already uses them), and raises a fill-in request for each missing secret (values never travel over MCP). If the review said adoptMode: true, call with adopt: true and NO resolutions to replace the files with the original's latest release wholesale — undoable via the safety checkpoint; confirm with your user first.

contents.description: The complete merged file for this conflict.

delete.description: True when the file should not exist after the update.

adopt.description: Only when the review reported adoptMode: true — replace the flow's files with the original's latest release wholesale.

note.description: One-line summary for the builder chat.

tools.name: flow_connect_chat
tools.title: Connect to an existing flow
tools.description: Attach this agent session to an EXISTING flow as a chat in the builder's rail (so the flow's owner sees your work alongside their own chats). Also use log_message to narrate what you're doing.

tools.name: flow_create_custom_table
tools.title: Create a custom data table
tools.description: Create a new custom data table (schema: name + typed columns) in your Final organization. USE THIS for any data the app must keep — loyalty stamps, waitlists, bookings, inventory logs, settings: the platform syncs the table to every station running the flow and keeps it working offline at the POS, so it replaces ANY browser-storage or hand-rolled persistence (localStorage/IndexedDB are forbidden and fail validate_flow). NEVER store credentials in a table — that's what the secrets vault (request_secret) is for. This creates the table IMMEDIATELY and ORG-WIDE (visible to every station and every flow, not just this one), so unless the user actually asked for stored data, confirm before creating; creation can also be plan-gated — surface a plan/permission error to the user rather than retrying. Check list_custom_tables first to reuse an existing table, and search_blueprints before building functionality around a new one: a selfPersisting blueprint brings its OWN tables by exact name and apply_blueprint_widgets provisions them for you, so a lookalike would sit dead while the feature keeps reading the real one. Create tables only for net-new data no applied blueprint persists. The name is normalized to kebab-case; generated code reads/writes rows via renderClient.getCustomTableData / upsertCustomTableData.

name.description: Table name; normalized to a kebab-case id, e.g. 'gift-cards'.
Column name.

referenceLinkedCollection.description: Foreign-key target collection (e.g. another custom table's kebab-case name).

referenceLinkedField.description: Foreign-key target field within that collection.

hubToken.description: Organization JWT fallback, only if the hub rejects your API key for this route.

tools.name: flow_create_flow
tools.title: Create a new flow
tools.description: Create a new, empty flow (app build) in your Final organization for YOU to write the app into. It appears in the Miami builder immediately, with this agent session attached as a chat. Optional theme knobs seed the live palette. Optional `device` ("mobile", "kiosk", "iphone", …) sets the preview frame it opens in; see set_flow_device. Returns the flow id and a builder deep link. Call get_scaffold before writing files. For an app the user merely DESCRIBED, use start_build.

agent.description: Display name for this tool in the builder chat rail, e.g. 'Claude Code'.

device.description: Default preview device for the new flow (the frame the builder opens it in). Omit for the user's Settings default.

anyOf.description: A device word: a surface (desktop, tablet, mobile, kiosk, kitchen-display, menu-board, drive-thru), a get_scaffold profile (portrait-handheld, counter-tablet, wall-kiosk, tv-display), or a skin (browser, macbook, ipad, iphone, android, kiosk, terminal, final-register, final-register-cfd, final-touch, final-touch-pro).

A full DeviceConfig: device (browser|macbook|ipad|iphone|android|kiosk|terminal|final-register|final-register-cfd|final-touch|final-touch-pro|custom), orientation (portrait|landscape), responsivePreset (desktop|tablet|mobile|custom), optional customWidth/customHeight.

color.description: A colour the user asked for, as they said it ("pink", "dark green", "navy and gold", or a hex). Resolved to a full custom palette for the flow's appearance — prefer this over guessing customColors hexes. Ignored when customColors is also given.

tools.name: flow_create_flow_from_blueprint
tools.title: Start a new build by copying an FBB
tools.description: Create a NEW flow that starts as a complete, vetted application rather than an empty file tree — the fastest path to a working build when an FBB (a Final Business Blueprint: a whole app) matches what the user wants. For an app the user merely DESCRIBED, use start_build (the website's own start picks the FBB); this verb is for when the user asked YOU to copy one. Find one with search_blueprints({ kind: "fbb" }). The app's screens, navigation and command-frame wiring are copied byte-exact from the build the FBB points at, its custom tables are re-created under THIS organization's names (the copied code already uses those names — keep them), and a fill-in request is raised for each secret it reads. This ALWAYS creates a new flow: an FBB cannot be merged into an existing build (there are no screen-graph merge semantics). To add parts to a build you already have, use apply_blueprint_widgets instead. THE COPY ENDS YOUR TURN. It is the finished deliverable, not step one — the app is vetted and already runs. When it returns, say its `report` line and stop: do NOT preview, validate, edit or extend it, and do not start on anything else the user described. The result names the tools not to call.

blueprintId.description: The exact FBB id, e.g. 'flow.coffee-quick-service'. An id without a version suffix resolves to the newest published version.

title.description: Name for the new flow. Defaults to the blueprint's title.

flowId.description: NOT SUPPORTED — passing this returns an error. An FBB replaces an app's entire screen graph, so it can only start a NEW build. It is declared here purely so a caller that assumes otherwise fails loudly instead of having the field stripped and getting a second flow it never asked for. To add parts to an existing build, use apply_blueprint_widgets({ flowId, picks }).

supersedesFlowId.description: The EMPTY placeholder flow you were told to build into, when a starter prompt pinned you to one before you knew an FBB would be used. This does NOT write into that flow — nothing can — it marks it as abandoned in favour of the flow created here, so the human's already-open builder tab follows you instead of watching an empty workspace forever. Pass the flow id from your instructions. Ignored (reported back as superseded:false) if that flow has any files, so it can never redirect a real build.

device.description: Override the copy's default preview device (the frame the builder opens it in): a surface word (mobile, tablet, kiosk, …), a get_scaffold profile, a skin (iphone, ipad, …) or a full DeviceConfig. Omit to follow the blueprint's surface. Changeable later with set_flow_device.

anyOf.description: A device word: a surface (desktop, tablet, mobile, kiosk, kitchen-display, menu-board, drive-thru), a get_scaffold profile (portrait-handheld, counter-tablet, wall-kiosk, tv-display), or a skin (browser, macbook, ipad, iphone, android, kiosk, terminal, final-register, final-register-cfd, final-touch, final-touch-pro).

A full DeviceConfig: device (browser|macbook|ipad|iphone|android|kiosk|terminal|final-register|final-register-cfd|final-touch|final-touch-pro|custom), orientation (portrait|landscape), responsivePreset (desktop|tablet|mobile|custom), optional customWidth/customHeight.

color.description: A colour the user asked for, as they said it ("pink", "dark green", "navy and gold", or a hex). Resolved to a full custom palette for the flow's appearance — prefer this over guessing customColors hexes. Ignored when customColors is also given.

tools.name: flow_delete_flow_files
tools.title: Delete files from a flow
tools.description: Remove files from a flow's tree by path. Engine-owned paths are rejected. Recorded as a checkpoint + chat note like writes.

tools.name: flow_deploy_flow
tools.title: Build and deploy a flow
tools.description: Direct deploy for CI/agent workflows: builds the app in a server sandbox (npm install + vite build) and publishes the dist to Final web-hosting as a new live version. Two things stop a deploy: a failing build, and a hardcoded credential (a build is distributable to other companies, so a baked-in secret would ship to all of them — use request_secret). Guardrail and type findings do NOT block; run validate_flow first if you want them. Omit `changelog` and the release notes are drafted for you from what changed since your last deploy — call log_message (or pass `note` on write_flow_files) as you work so those notes describe intent rather than just file names. Uses your organization's provisioned hub credential automatically (the same long-term org JWT the extension tools use) — no token argument needed once you've connected. Pass `hostingToken` only as an escape hatch to override it; if no credential is available, reconnect via the Connect dialog or use open_in_builder and deploy from the Launch tool instead.

hostingToken.description: Organization JWT accepted by hosting.finalpos.com. Optional escape hatch — omit to use your organization's stored hub credential (the same long-term org JWT the extension tools use).

tools.name: flow_get_blueprint
tools.title: Inspect one blueprint's code
tools.description: INSPECTION ONLY — read a blueprint's overlay code by id (from list_blueprints) to understand how it works. To USE a blueprint, apply it: apply_blueprint_widgets for a widget-set (materializes its widgets byte-exact with the command-frame plumbing intact AND provisions the custom tables its code depends on), create_flow_from_blueprint for an FBB. Do NOT re-type code from this tool into write_flow_files — that silently drops the vetted plumbing and leaves its tables unprovisioned. `tables` (when present) lists the custom tables the code binds to by exact name. For a WHOLE-FLOW blueprint this returns the screen manifest WITHOUT file bytes by default — an entire app is far too large to read this way, and you never need to: instantiation copies it server-side. Pass includeFiles: true only to audit the source.

tools.name: flow_get_preview_status
tools.title: Check preview health + logs
tools.description: Authoritative server-side health probe of the flow's preview sandbox, plus a short snapshot of recent dev-server logs (useful to diagnose a red screen or crash).

tools.name: flow_get_scaffold
tools.title: Get the app scaffold contract
tools.description: The contract every Final flow app is built against: which files the ENGINE owns (never write them — they are re-asserted verbatim), the baseline package.json (Vite + React 19 + TS + Tailwind + command-frame), the rules your files must follow, and the runtime contracts that compile and preview fine but fail on a real device (money in minor units, the first-load handshake, getX response unwrapping, tender success semantics). Call this once before writing any files; pass `device` for layout guidance.

device.description: Target surface — "portrait-handheld", "counter-tablet", "wall-kiosk" or "tv-display". Approximate words work ("kiosk", "phone", "menu board"); an unrecognized value just returns the device-agnostic contract.

tools.name: flow_get_upstream_status
tools.title: Check a clone for upstream updates
tools.description: Has the build this flow was copied from released a newer version? Covers both a "Make it yours" clone of a listing and a build started from an FBB. Returns update.status: "available" (a newer deployed release exists — review it with get_upstream_update), "current" (up to date), "unknown" (the original has no comparable release), or "gone" (the original was DELETED — for a share clone, also if it was un-shared; an FBB's parent stays reachable while it exists, because the catalog vouches for it rather than the owner's share toggle), with the release notes published since the copy. Flows that are not snapshot-sourced copies return update: null. Cheap — safe to call whenever the user asks about updates.

tools.name: flow_get_upstream_update
tools.title: Review a pending upstream update
tools.description: Review what an update from the original build would change — the same review the builder shows its maker, shaped for an agent. Returns the releases since the clone, the clean changes (added/changed/removed paths, with full incoming contents for added+changed), and CONFLICTS: files where this flow's own edits and the update collide, each with complete base/ours/theirs contents. RESOLUTION CONTRACT (match the builder's behavior): when both sides' changes serve different purposes, merge them yourself — one file keeping BOTH sides' improvements; never wholesale-pick a side out of convenience. ONLY when the two sides genuinely contradict on the same visible thing (a color, a layout, a label, a behavior) ask YOUR user which they want, in plain product language — describe the visible difference, never file names or code. Then call apply_upstream_update with exactly one resolution per conflict. The trees you see are already in THIS organization's table namespace — never rename tableName literals yourself. adoptMode: true means the merge base is unrecoverable, so no merge is possible: offer the user adopting the latest release wholesale (apply_upstream_update with adopt: true) or staying put. upToDate: true means there is nothing to do.

tools.name: flow_install_extension
tools.title: Install an extension org-wide
tools.description: Install an extension ORG-WIDE: creates the install link on EVERY company in your Final organization (demo companies included), skipping companies that already have it, so it is safe to retry. Installing is deliberate and org-visible — confirm with your user and call this ONLY when they explicitly asked for the extension. Find the id with list_extensions (organization and public extensions both install); after a successful install the extension's surfaces become embeddable — inspect them with list_extension_surfaces and build the ones carrying requirementsMd natively instead of embedding. Per-company failures are collected in the result rather than thrown, and `installState` reports the org-wide outcome (installed / partial / none).

extensionId.description: The extension's id (the `id` from a list_extensions result — org or public source).

hubToken.description: Organization JWT fallback, only if the hub rejects your API key for this route.

tools.name: flow_list_blueprints
tools.title: List the blueprint catalog
tools.description: List EVERY vetted, type-checked blueprint available to reuse — working functionality (gift cards, loyalty, payment surfaces, product grids, carts, customer views, order tickets, receipts), not just screen layouts. Check the catalog BEFORE creating custom tables or hand-rolling a capability. Returns id, kind, slot, title, summary, surfaces, tags, and selfPersisting per blueprint — selfPersisting: true means it reads/writes its OWN custom tables by exact name inside its code, which applying then provisions in your organization automatically (some are extension-owned and come from installing that extension); never create a table for a feature it covers. TWO KINDS, used differently: kind "widget-set" (the default this returns) is a set of parts you copy into an existing build with apply_blueprint_widgets; kind "fbb" is a Final Business Blueprint — a COMPLETE APP. It has no widgets to copy and is used with create_flow_from_blueprint to start a NEW flow. Pass kind: "fbb" to browse complete apps, or kind: "any" for both. To find the best match for a specific capability instead of scanning the whole catalog, use search_blueprints. get_blueprint is read-only inspection.

tools.name: flow_list_custom_tables
tools.title: List the org's custom data tables
tools.description: List your organization's custom data tables with their column schemas. Custom tables are Final's built-in, station-syncing database — data written on one station is automatically synced to every other station running the flow, and keeps working OFFLINE at the point of sale. They are the ONLY sanctioned persistence for generated apps (browser storage is per-device, never syncs, and is wiped on real Render terminals — validate_flow rejects it). Call this before create_custom_table to reuse an existing table instead of duplicating one. For NEW functionality, check search_blueprints before designing tables — a vetted blueprint may already provide the feature, and a selfPersisting blueprint's tables may NOT appear in this list (often extension-owned, resolved by name at runtime): their absence is never a reason to create lookalikes. Generated code reads/writes rows at runtime via renderClient.getCustomTableData / upsertCustomTableData (ground with lookup_command_frame).

hubToken.description: Organization JWT fallback, only if the hub rejects your API key for this route.

tools.name: flow_list_extension_custom_tables
tools.title: List an extension's custom tables
tools.description: List the CUSTOM TABLES an extension registers (table name + typed columns), so generated code can read/write its data at runtime via renderClient.getCustomTableData / upsertCustomTableData by table name (ground the calls with lookup_command_frame). Only the org's OWN extensions expose their tables — a public / other-org extension returns an empty list with a note. Pass the extension's id from list_extensions; the org's non-extension tables come from list_custom_tables. Read-only. Does not write files.

extensionId.description: The extension's id (the `id` from a list_extensions result).

hubToken.description: Organization JWT fallback, only if the hub rejects your API key for this route.

tools.name: flow_list_extension_surfaces
tools.title: List an extension's surfaces
tools.description: List the SURFACES an extension exposes — embeddable iframe injection points, each with a surfaceId, a platform (builder/hub/render), a type, and a url. Render an installed surface inside a generated screen with the engine component `<ExtensionSurface surfaceId="<surfaceId>" />` (ground it with lookup_engine_component). A surface may carry `requirementsMd` — full markdown build instructions for re-implementing it NATIVELY in the app: when present, prefer building that surface as first-class native screens in the app's own styling with real command-frame wiring, and embed `<ExtensionSurface>` only for surfaces without it. Works for the org's own extensions (hub credential) and public ones (resolved via the public marketplace, no credential needed). Pass the extension's id from list_extensions. Read-only. Does not write files.

extensionId.description: The extension's id (the `id` from a list_extensions result).

hubToken.description: Organization JWT fallback, only if the hub rejects your API key for this route.

tools.name: flow_list_extensions
tools.title: List available extensions
tools.description: List the platform EXTENSIONS available to your organization — the org's own plus the public marketplace — so you can suggest, inspect, or install one. Each entry carries an id, label, category, short description, and its source (organization or public); public results need no hub credential, and a note tells you when the org-owned side was unavailable. Pass query with the capability the user asked for — results are relevance-ranked against it (label, category, and the vocabulary of the blueprints each extension enables) and capped to the genuine matches, so an empty list means NO extension provides that capability. Omit query to browse the whole catalog with skip/limit paging — publicTotal reports how many marketplace rows exist. Inspect a result with list_extension_surfaces / list_extension_custom_tables; install it org-wide with install_extension ONLY when your user explicitly asked for it. Read-only. Does not write files.

query.description: The capability the user asked for, in their own words (e.g. 'loyalty points', 'age gate', 'gift card') — results are relevance-ranked and capped to genuine matches. Omit to browse the org's own plus the first public page.

hubToken.description: Organization JWT fallback, only if the hub rejects your API key for this route.

tools.name: flow_list_flows
tools.title: List your flows
tools.description: List the flows (app builds) in your organization, newest first: id, title, timestamps, and live theme knobs. Final staff sessions also see Final's own flows, marked owner: "Final". Use a flow id with the other tools, or create_flow to start fresh. Clones of listed builds carry an upstreamUpdate field when the build they were copied from has released a newer version — review and apply it with get_upstream_update / apply_upstream_update.

tools.name: flow_list_secret_keys
tools.title: List stored secret key names
tools.description: List the key NAMES already stored in your organization's encrypted secrets vault — never the values (no tool returns a secret value). Use this to (a) reuse an existing key instead of requesting a new one, and (b) poll whether a request_secret ask has been fulfilled by the human. Generated code reads a secret at RUNTIME with renderClient.getSecretVal({ key }) — the build ships key names only.

hubToken.description: Organization JWT fallback, only if the hub rejects your API key for this route.

tools.name: flow_log_message
tools.title: Log a message to the flow's chat
tools.description: Record a message in this agent's chat inside the builder — the user's request (role 'user') or your own progress/summary (role 'assistant'). Keeps the builder timeline faithful to what happened in this session.

tools.name: flow_lookup_command_frame
tools.title: Look up command-frame API
tools.description: Look up the EXACT, version-locked command-frame API a generated Final POS app runs on: renderClient method signatures + params, CF* entity field lists, pub/sub topic event vocabularies, and worked examples. Pass one of method/entity/topic for a precise lookup, entity+field to confirm a field exists, query for fuzzy search, or the plural batch forms. Ground every renderClient call in this before writing it — fabricated fields/methods fail on real Render devices. Typed signatures and entity fields are authoritative; the worked examples come from upstream docs and are NOT typechecked, so where they disagree, trust the types. Results carry `traps` for known field-level gotchas.

tools.name: flow_lookup_engine_component
tools.title: Look up engine helper components
tools.description: Look up the exact props/signature of an engine-owned `./final/*` helper: the `@/final/ui` primitives (Button, IconButton, Card, Tile, Input, Field, Chip, ListRow, Dialog, Sheet, Toolbar, Heading, EmptyState, cn) plus usePrint, StationHomeButton, SwitchUserButton, useStationHome, Barcode, BootSplash. These are re-asserted into every generated app — compose screens from the primitives (see get_scaffold contracts.designLadder) and import the rest instead of hand-rolling buttons/cards/dialogs, printing, station-home/switch-user, barcodes, or the loading splash. Pass name for a precise lookup, query for fuzzy search, or neither to list all.

tools.name: flow_lookup_pos_api
tools.title: Look up Final POS REST API
tools.description: Look up the Final POS REST API (https://api.finalpos.com) — endpoint method/path, request fields, response shape, and a worked fetch example. This is the ONLINE-ONLY fallback for admin/management operations command-frame cannot express (creating products/variants/categories, customer management, outlets/stations/tax tables, webhooks). Command-frame is ALWAYS first choice for live POS data — it works offline and the host owns money/totals. A call to this API is network egress from the station: it fails whenever connectivity does, so never put one in the sale path — use it for setup/admin work and degrade gracefully. Pass resource to list a domain, operation for one endpoint, or query for fuzzy search.

tools.name: flow_open_in_builder
tools.title: Get the builder hand-off link
tools.description: The recommended way to finish: a deep link that opens this flow in the Miami builder, where the owner can review the work, restore checkpoints, and deploy through the Launch tool (validation gates, listing media, changelog, version history).

tools.name: flow_read_flow_files
tools.title: Read a flow's files
tools.description: Read a flow's generated source tree. Omit `paths` to list all file paths (cheap); pass `paths` to fetch specific files' contents.

tools.name: flow_rename_flow
tools.title: Rename a flow
tools.description: Rename a build (flow) authoritatively across the platform in one call: the builder header, list_flows / open_in_builder, and the Deerlake catalog all reflect the new title, and updatedAt is bumped. A deployed build keeps its hosted web app: the hostname and version history are unchanged, and the next deploy_flow publishes the next version. Does NOT edit the app source: rename a hardcoded old name yourself with write_flow_files.

tools.name: flow_request_secret
tools.title: Ask the human to store a secret
tools.description: Ask the flow's owner to enter a third-party credential (API key, auth token, webhook secret) into Final's encrypted vault. THIS TOOL TAKES NO VALUE and no tool ever returns one — the human types it into a masked input in the Miami builder, and it goes straight into the vault. Why: flow builds are DISTRIBUTABLE to other companies, so a credential must never be baked into the code (validate_flow and deploy_flow scan for and block hardcoded secrets). Your generated code reads it at RUNTIME with renderClient.getSecretVal({ key }) and must degrade gracefully while the key isn't stored yet (disable the integration + tell the user to configure it — never crash). After calling this: tell YOUR user to open the builder link and enter the value, and poll list_secret_keys to detect when it lands.

key.description: Kebab-case vault key the code will read, e.g. 'twilio-auth-token'.

label.description: Human label shown in the builder, e.g. 'Twilio Auth Token'.

reason.description: Why the app needs this credential.

docsUrl.description: Where the user can find/generate the credential.

hubToken.description: Organization JWT fallback, only if the hub rejects your API key for this route.

tools.name: flow_search_blueprints
tools.title: Search the blueprint catalog
tools.description: SEMANTIC search over the vetted blueprint catalog — matches are ranked by what you MEAN, not by shared words, so describe the capability in plain language ('rewards for repeat customers' finds the loyalty blueprint). RUN THIS FIRST — before creating custom tables or hand-rolling a capability: blueprints ship working FUNCTIONALITY (gift cards, loyalty, payment surfaces, carts), not just screen layouts. Search once per FEATURE you're adding (smart grid, gift cards, loyalty points, receipts) and REPEAT it for each distinct capability rather than issuing one broad query — a build usually combines several. Returns { results, note? }: blueprint summaries (id, slot, title, summary, surfaces, tags, selfPersisting, match score in [0,1]) best match first. selfPersisting: true means the blueprint reads/writes its OWN custom tables by exact name inside its code, and apply_blueprint_widgets provisions them in your organization automatically (extension-owned ones come from installing that extension) — NEVER create a table for a feature it covers. Prefer this over list_blueprints when you know what you need. Pick the widgets you need and copy them with apply_blueprint_widgets({ flowId, picks }) — applied ON TOP of the current build, never replacing it. Low match scores across the board mean no vetted blueprint fits — only then build that piece from scratch grounded in the command-frame docs. Optional `slot`/`surface` narrow the results; `limit` caps how many are returned (default 10).

tools.name: flow_start_preview
tools.title: Start (or sync) the live preview
tools.description: Boot the flow's server-side preview sandbox (Vite dev server) — or reconcile a running one to the flow's current files — and return its public HTTPS URL already pinned to this flow's mock dataset: the maker's pick, else its vertical's (sushi, not restaurant). Open the URL in a browser to see the app; call again after write_flow_files to sync. Previews idle-stop on their own; call stop_preview when done to free resources sooner.

tools.name: flow_stop_preview
tools.title: Stop the preview
tools.description: Stop the flow's preview sandbox and free its resources. The next start_preview cold-boots in a couple of seconds.

tools.name: flow_sync_preview
tools.title: Sync the preview to the flow's files
tools.description: Reconcile a (running or cold) preview sandbox to the flow's current files and run the green-build gate (tsc + vite build). Returns the gate result — the fastest way to know your code actually compiles. The engine forces parts of package.json on every sync: the dev/build/typecheck scripts, and the vendored command-frame + mock packages to their bundled tarballs. Baseline and build dependencies are re-added only when you declared them nowhere, so your own additions and pins survive. Shares one rate bucket with start_preview — sync once per change-set, not per file.

tools.name: flow_update_custom_table
tools.title: Change a custom table's schema
tools.description: Evolve an EXISTING custom data table's schema: add columns, change existing ones (rename/retype — destructive for stored rows, use sparingly), or drop columns. The table is identified by its kebab-case name from list_custom_tables. Tables are ORG-WIDE, so a schema change lands for every flow and station already using this one — check who reads it before reshaping. NEVER rename or reshape a table a selfPersisting blueprint reads/writes — its copied code references the exact current names. Per-operation failures are collected rather than aborting the whole change. Row data itself stays a runtime concern of the generated app (renderClient).

tableName.description: The existing table's kebab-case name (see list_custom_tables).

name.description: Column name.

referenceLinkedCollection.description: Foreign-key target collection (e.g. another custom table's kebab-case name).

referenceLinkedField.description: Foreign-key target field within that collection.

name.description: The existing column to change.

newName.description: Rename (orphans row data stored under the old key).

removeFields.description: Columns to drop (destructive: their data is removed).

hubToken.description: Organization JWT fallback, only if the hub rejects your API key for this route.

tools.name: flow_validate_flow
tools.title: Validate a flow against the platform contract
tools.description: Deterministic STATIC checks against the platform contract: (1) guardrails — fabricated renderClient methods, forbidden browser APIs/imports, engine-file writes; (2) a REAL TypeScript check of command-frame usage against the PINNED .d.ts the app installs (the version is stamped in the result) — this proves TYPES, never runtime behaviour and never device parity; (3) a hardcoded-credentials scan; (4) `flowTypeErrors` — a whole-tree `tsc` against REAL react types, which catches what (2) cannot see (e.g. a `useEffect` cleanup that returns a value, a hard TS2345 the builder's in-chat gate will report to whoever opens this flow); plus advisory `warnings` (client money math, hardcoded catalog data, missing station-home/data-test, tip-as-cart-fee) that don't affect `clean` but each predict a real on-device failure. secretFindings BLOCK deploy_flow; everything else is advisory. Run it after each write batch, before start_preview.

tools.name: flow_write_flow_files
tools.title: Write files into a flow
tools.description: Create or overwrite files in a flow's tree (full contents, not diffs). Engine-owned paths are rejected — see get_scaffold. Every write lands as a restorable checkpoint and is narrated in the builder chat. If a live preview is running, follow up with start_preview to sync it. Validate with validate_flow before deploying. If a call returns an error the files may STILL have landed (and a very large payload can truncate mid-file) — re-read with read_flow_files before retrying, never blind-retry. Because writes replace whole files, keep files small and single-purpose so an edit can't clobber unrelated working code.

note.description: One-line summary of the change, shown in the builder chat.

tools.name: get_connection
tools.title: About this connection
tools.description: Who this connection acts as: organisation, user, the company Hub tools act on and the companies you may switch to, the allowed and listed packs, and how to reach tools that are not listed.

tools.name: hub_add_customer_note
tools.title: Add customer note
tools.description: Add a note to a customer — an allergy, a preference, what happened with an order. Existing notes are KEPT; this appends. Takes the customer ID from get_customers. Staff read these in the cabinet, so write what the merchant said, not your own summary.

customerId.description: Customer id from get_customers — not a name

tools.name: hub_add_modifier_choice
tools.title: Add a choice
tools.description: Add one choice to an existing modifier, leaving the rest alone. This is the safe way to extend a modifier — unlike update_modifier, it cannot drop anything. Appends to the end unless sortOrder says otherwise. price is the extra charge per unit as a human amount ("0.70"); omit it for a choice that costs nothing, which still prints on the receipt.

name.description: What the cashier sees, e.g. "Oat milk"

price.description: Extra charge per unit, e.g. "0.70". Omit or "0" for a choice that costs nothing

isDefault.description: Pre-selected at the till. On "Pick one" at most one choice may have it

sortOrder.description: Position in the list. Omit to append

unavailableOutletIds.description: Outlets where this choice is NOT sold (an exception list — omit or [] means sold everywhere). Outlet ids from get_outlets

tools.name: hub_add_product_images
tools.title: Add product images
tools.description: Add photos to an existing product — from public URLs, or as base64 bytes when the merchant attached the file itself and there is no URL. URL images are downloaded and stored on the platform, so the product never depends on someone else's site staying up. Existing photos are KEPT — this adds to them. JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF/HEIC, up to 20MB each. Takes the product ID from get_products, never a name.

productId.description: Product id from get_products — not a name

imageUrls.description: Public URLs of the photos to add

imageFiles.description: Photos the merchant attached — use when there is no public URL

tools.name: hub_add_tax_rate_to_group
tools.title: Add rate to group
tools.description: Add an EXISTING rate to a tax group, or change that rate’s compounding flag within the group. Both ids come from get_taxes. This shares the rate — it does not copy it. The group starts charging the rate’s existing per-outlet percentages, and a later edit to that rate changes this group too. Use create_tax_rate instead when the rate does not exist yet. The rate is appended last in the charging order; use update_tax_group with rateIdsInOrder to move it. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT — this immediately adds tax to every product in the group. Sales already rung up are NOT recalculated — this only affects sales from now on.

taxRateId.description: Tax rate id from get_taxes — an existing rate, shared not copied

compounding.description: Charge this rate on the running total including the rates above it. Default false

tools.name: hub_adjust_stock
tools.title: Adjust stock
tools.description: Change the count of ONE variant at ONE outlet — the cabinet's "Adjust Inventory" action. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT FIRST, repeating the product, the outlet, the reason and the number: this writes immediately, is permanently recorded against the employee in the stock history, and there is no undo from here. Reasons: STOCK_RECEIVED (a delivery arrived) and RESTOCK_RETURN (a return put back on the shelf) ADD the quantity; DAMAGE, THEFT and LOSS SUBTRACT it; INVENTORY_RECOUNT SETS the count to exactly the quantity you pass (a physical stocktake). Always pass quantity as a positive number — the reason decides the direction. Pick the reason the merchant actually gave; these end up in reports, so recording theft as damage misstates their loss. If stock is not tracked for that variant at that outlet, NOTHING is written and the result says applied: false — do not report success, and do not read it as "the stock is 0". Tracking has to be turned on for the product first. To move units between outlets use create_stock_transfer instead.

variantId.description: Variant id from get_products — the exact variant being counted

outletId.description: Outlet id from get_outlets — the adjustment applies only there

action.description: Why the count changed. Adds: STOCK_RECEIVED, RESTOCK_RETURN. Subtracts: DAMAGE, THEFT, LOSS. Sets: INVENTORY_RECOUNT

quantity.description: Always positive. Units added or removed — or, for INVENTORY_RECOUNT, the new total on hand

tools.name: hub_assign_role
tools.title: Assign role
tools.description: Move a team member onto a different role — this is how someone gains or loses access. Answers 'give Maria access to the reports', 'make him a cashier again', 'take away her permissions'. PERMISSIONS ARE POWER. Confirm with the merchant first, naming the person and the role out loud ("give Maria the Manager role — yes?"), and never act on a role change you inferred rather than were asked for. The change is live on the next request: rights are re-read from the role every time, so no one logs out and no agent key stops working — including yours, if the change reaches your own account. It swaps their WHOLE permission set for that role’s, so read get_roles first and check the new role really carries what the merchant asked for and nothing dangerous besides — if no existing role fits, say so rather than picking the closest one. You may also point the merchant’s own account at another role, including the account this agent key belongs to, which would change your own permissions from the next call onward: never do that unless the merchant asked for it in those words. To change what a role itself allows, without moving anyone, use update_role.

userId.description: User id from get_team — not a name

roleId.description: Role id from get_roles — not a role name

tools.name: hub_cancel_booking
tools.title: Cancel a booking
tools.description: Release a booked window. The order stays as it is — cancelling a booking is not a refund, and money is never moved here; if the customer is owed money, do that on the order. Confirm with the merchant before cancelling a booking somebody already paid for.

tools.name: hub_cancel_purchase_order
tools.title: Cancel purchase order
tools.description: Cancel an order the merchant no longer wants. CONFIRM FIRST, naming the supplier and the PO number — there is no undo, and the order disappears from the list rather than showing as cancelled. REFUSED once any stock has been received against it: that stock is real and the record has to stay. Receive the rest instead, or leave it partially received. Cancelling does NOT tell the supplier anything. If the order was already sent, the merchant still has to contact them — say so.

purchaseOrderId.description: Purchase order id from get_purchase_orders — not a PO number

tools.name: hub_confirm_booking
tools.title: Confirm a held booking
tools.description: Turn a hold into a real booking once the order behind it is paid, so it stops expiring. Needs the order the booking was sold on — confirming without one is refused, because a confirmed booking nobody can find on a receipt is worse than an expired hold.

orderId.description: The paid order carrying this booking

tools.name: hub_create_booking_resource
tools.title: Create a booking resource
tools.description: Add one bookable thing to the company directory. Call get_booking_resources first — a resource is reused across every service, so a second "Marco" would split one barber into two calendars and let him be booked twice at once. The name is what staff will see in the calendar.

name.description: As the merchant says it, e.g. "Marco", "Room 101", "Scooter 7"

kind.description: What sort of thing it is — drives the labels the merchant sees

tag.description: Identifier of this exact instance if it has one: room number, plate, QR, e.g. "SC-07"

tools.name: hub_create_booking_rules
tools.title: Create a booking rule set
tools.description: Create a booking policy. Call get_booking_rules FIRST and reuse a matching set instead — these are shared company-wide, not per product. `weeklyHours` are LOCAL wall-clock times at the outlet; if neither the outlet nor the company has a timezone the engine refuses availability with a 400, so fix the outlet rather than guessing an offset. `bufferMinutes` consumes grid time for slot bookings (cleaning between appointments); for overnight stays use checkInTime/checkOutTime instead and leave the buffer at 0 — the cleaning window lives in the gap and does not consume a night.

name.description: How the merchant refers to it, e.g. "Haircuts 9–18"

bookingType.description: appointment = a person's time; rental = an asset; overnight = nights; group = a class

ratePeriod.description: What ONE unit of price buys. `slot` for appointments and hourly rental. `week` and `month` are in the enum but NOT offered: the grid still cuts them one day at a time, so a weekly rate would be charged per day

weeklyHours.description: Opening hours per weekday, local time. Days left out are closed. For overnight stays leave hours off only if the property has none — an empty list there means every day.

slotLengthMinutes.description: How long one booking lasts, e.g. 30

bufferMinutes.description: Dead time after each booking, e.g. 15 for cleaning. Consumes the grid

holdMinutes.description: How long an unpaid hold survives before the window frees itself. Default 10

maxAdvanceDays.description: How far ahead bookings open. 0 = no limit

tools.name: hub_create_category
tools.title: Create category
tools.description: Create a product category. Call get_categories FIRST — a second "Drinks" is easy to make and there is no merge. Pass parentId to make it a subcategory; leave it out for a top-level one. The cabinet's own form asks for a description, so ask the merchant for one rather than inventing it. This does NOT move any product into the category — do that with update_product and its categoryIds.

name.description: Category name as the merchant said it, e.g. "Beverages"

description.description: Short description shown in the cabinet

image.description: Image URL, or a Lucide icon reference like "lucide:coffee"

parentId.description: Parent category id from get_categories — a name is rejected. Omit for top level

sortOrder.description: Position among its siblings, lowest first. Omit to leave it unsorted

tools.name: hub_create_customer
tools.title: Create customer
tools.description: Create a customer. Call get_customers with the email or name FIRST — a duplicate splits one person’s order history in two and there is no merge from here. Email is required, exactly as in the cabinet's own customer form. Ask the merchant for anything you do not know instead of inventing it — an invented phone number or address is worse than a missing one.

phone.description: Phone as the merchant said it, e.g. "+1 555 123 4567"

shipping.description: Shipping address. Omit to reuse the billing address

note.description: A first note about this customer, if the merchant gave one

tools.name: hub_create_modifier
tools.title: Create modifier
tools.description: Create a new question the till can ask, with its choices. THIS ALONE DOES NOTHING AT THE TILL — follow it with link_modifier_to_category, or the modifier sits unused. Choose selectionType carefully, because it CANNOT be changed afterwards: "single" = pick exactly one (milk, cooking temperature); "multiple" = tick any number of different choices (toppings); "multiple" with allowQuantity true = tick choices AND say how many of each; "quantity" = every choice is a stepper (extra shots). The last two count UNITS, not distinct choices. allowQuantity is only accepted on "multiple" and is refused on the others. Names must be unique for the merchant, ignoring case.

name.description: What the cashier sees, e.g. "Milk" or "Toppings"

selectionType.description: How it is answered. CANNOT be changed later

allowQuantity.description: Only with selectionType "multiple": let each ticked choice carry a count. CANNOT be changed later

choices.description: The choices. Can also be added later one at a time

name.description: What the cashier sees, e.g. "Oat milk"

price.description: Extra charge per unit, e.g. "0.70". Omit or "0" for a choice that costs nothing

isDefault.description: Pre-selected at the till. On "Pick one" at most one choice may have it

sortOrder.description: Position in the list. Omit to append

unavailableOutletIds.description: Outlets where this choice is NOT sold (an exception list — omit or [] means sold everywhere). Outlet ids from get_outlets

tools.name: hub_create_outlet
tools.title: Create outlet
tools.description: Open a new point of sale — the cabinet’s Add Outlet form. Name and the full street address (address, city, state, postCode) are all REQUIRED, exactly as on that form. Do NOT try to set a country: every outlet inherits the company’s country, and it can never be changed per outlet. Ask the merchant for any part of the address you do not know — an invented address ends up on receipts. This is BILLABLE: a new outlet counts against the company plan’s outlet allowance and the call is refused once that allowance is used up. Confirm with the merchant before calling. Afterwards the platform seeds a stock row of 0 for every product at the new outlet in the background, so its stock reads as empty until someone receives or transfers stock in. Linking a Stripe account to the outlet is NOT possible from here — the merchant does that in Settings → Outlets.

name.description: Outlet name as the merchant calls it, e.g. "King Street"

address.description: Street address, e.g. "123 King St W"

taxId.description: Business tax number printed on this outlet’s receipts (BN / GST / HST / VAT / EIN)

alias.description: Short code used by the WooCommerce / Metorik integration. Can never be changed once set — leave it out unless the merchant asked for it

tools.name: hub_create_product
tools.title: Create product
tools.description: Create a product in the merchant's catalogue. Call get_products first to make sure it does not already exist. Prices are HUMAN strings like "19.99" — this tool converts them into the company's currency itself, so never send cents. Tax: the company's standard tax table is applied by default; pass taxable:false for an untaxed product. Ask the merchant for anything you do not know instead of inventing it.

name.description: Product name as the merchant said it

productType.description: Only pass this for "booking" — a service sold as TIME (a haircut, a room for the night, an hour on a scooter). simple/variable are derived from `options`, so leave it out for goods. A booking product is not bookable until set_product_booking_setup gives it a rule set and resources.

price.description: Selling price as a human string, e.g. "19.99"

costPrice.description: What the merchant pays for it, human string

barcode.description: EAN/UPC if the merchant gave one

options.description: Variation axes and the values to build variants from, e.g. {"Size":["Small","Large"]}. Every combination becomes a variant. Call get_product_options FIRST and reuse existing axes. Every variant gets `price` unless variantPrices says otherwise.

variantPrices.description: Per-variant prices at creation, one entry per combination that differs from `price`, e.g. {"options":{"Size":"Large"},"price":"21.99"}. `options` must name one value for EVERY axis in `options`.

taxable.description: Default true: applies the standard tax table

taxTableId.description: A specific tax table, for non-standard tax

tools.name: hub_create_product_option
tools.title: Create product option
tools.description: Create a new variation axis with its possible values. Use it only when get_product_options shows nothing suitable. The axis is shared across the whole catalogue, not one product — so confirm the name and values with the merchant first and reuse an existing axis when one fits.

name.description: Axis name as the merchant says it, e.g. "Size"

values.description: Possible values in display order, e.g. ["Small","Medium","Large"]

tools.name: hub_create_purchase_order
tools.title: Create purchase order
tools.description: Write a new order to a supplier. It is created as a DRAFT — nothing reaches the supplier and no stock moves until send_purchase_order. PREREQUISITES, in this order: get_suppliers for the supplierId, get_outlets for the outlet the goods will be delivered INTO, then get_supplier_items WITH that outletId for the lines — variantId and unitCost come from there, and an item that is not linked to this supplier is refused. unitCost is what the merchant pays per unit as a human amount ("12.50"), prefilled from the supplier link but editable if this order was negotiated differently. quantity is in the item’s selling unit and may be fractional for goods sold by weight or length. Read the lines back to the merchant with the total before sending — a wrong quantity here becomes wrong stock later.

outletId.description: Outlet id from get_outlets — where the goods will be received

variantId.description: Item id from get_supplier_items — the supplier must carry it

quantity.description: How many, in the unit the item is sold in. May be fractional for goods sold by weight or length

unitCost.description: Cost per unit the merchant pays, e.g. "12.50". Never cents, never the selling price

discount.description: Flat discount on this line, e.g. "2.00". Not with discountPercent

discountPercent.description: Discount as a percentage of this line’s goods

feePerUnit.description: Extra cost per unit on this line

expectedDate.description: ISO date the merchant expects delivery

notes.description: Note for the supplier / for the merchant’s own records

discount.description: Flat discount on the whole order, e.g. "25.00". Not with discountPercent

discountPercent.description: Discount as a percentage of the items subtotal

shippingFee.description: Shipping charged on the order, e.g. "18.00"

dutyFees.description: Duty / customs charged on the order

customFees.description: Any other named charge on the order, e.g. "Handling"

tools.name: hub_create_role
tools.title: Create role
tools.description: Create a new role with a chosen set of permissions — for when no existing role fits what the merchant wants someone to do. Check get_roles first; a near-match plus update_role is usually better than a fourth almost-identical role. PERMISSIONS ARE POWER. Confirm with the merchant first, naming the person and the role out loud ("give Maria the Manager role — yes?"), and never act on a role change you inferred rather than were asked for. The change is live on the next request: rights are re-read from the role every time, so no one logs out and no agent key stops working — including yours, if the change reaches your own account. Permission ids come from get_permissions. List back in plain words what the role will be able to do and get an explicit yes before calling. Creating a role gives nobody anything until assign_role puts a person on it. If you are signed in as an employee you can only grant permissions you hold yourself — the cabinet works the same way — and the call is refused otherwise.

name.description: What the merchant calls it, e.g. "Shift lead"

permissionIds.description: Permission ids from get_permissions — everything not listed is switched off

tools.name: hub_create_station
tools.title: Add virtual till
tools.description: Add a VIRTUAL till — a browser-based station, the cabinet’s "Add Virtual Station". It is created at one outlet and starts AVAILABLE. You CANNOT create a native (device) station from here and must not try: a physical till enrols itself when someone opens the POS app on the device and names it there. THIS IS BILLABLE — a new station counts against the company plan’s station allowance and the call is refused once that allowance is used up. Confirm with the merchant before calling. flowSrcId is the POS layout the till runs. The cabinet’s wizard makes picking one mandatory and there is no tool here that lists flows, so unless the merchant gave you an id, create the station and then tell them plainly to open Run → Stations and choose the flow — until they do, the station exists but cannot be launched.

name.description: Station name as staff will see it, e.g. "POS 2"

outletId.description: Which outlet this till belongs to — id from get_outlets, not a name

flowSrcId.description: Id of the POS layout (flow) the till runs, if the merchant gave one

tools.name: hub_create_stock_transfer
tools.title: Send stock transfer
tools.description: Move stock from one outlet to another — 'send 10 of these from the warehouse to the King Street shop'. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT FIRST, naming both outlets and every quantity: this writes immediately and there is no undo from here. The stock LEAVES the source outlet at once; the destination only gains it when someone confirms arrival with receive_stock_transfer, so until then those units are in transit and count in neither shop. Tell the merchant that. Variant ids come from get_products, outlet ids from get_outlets. Check availability with get_stock first: sending more than the source holds is rejected, and so is sending a variant whose stock is not tracked at the source — there is no count there to move. To correct a count in place (damage, theft, a recount) use adjust_stock instead; to book in a supplier delivery use adjust_stock with STOCK_RECEIVED.

fromOutletId.description: Source outlet id from get_outlets — stock leaves here immediately

toOutletId.description: Destination outlet id from get_outlets — must differ from the source

quantity.description: Units to send — must not exceed what the source holds

items.description: What to move. One entry per variant

invoice.description: Invoice or reference number, if the merchant gave one

note.description: A note staff will read on the transfer

tools.name: hub_create_supplier
tools.title: Create supplier
tools.description: Add a business the merchant buys from. Only the name is required, and it must be unique among this company’s suppliers. Set contactEmail if the merchant will ever email purchase orders to this supplier — send_purchase_order has nowhere to send without it. A brand-new supplier carries NO items, so it cannot be ordered from yet: link its items with link_supplier_items before creating a purchase order. Ask the merchant for details you do not have rather than inventing them — this ends up on the orders their supplier reads.

name.description: Supplier name as the merchant calls it

notes.description: Free-text notes, e.g. delivery days or account number

tools.name: hub_create_tax_group
tools.title: Create tax group
tools.description: Create an empty tax group (a tax profile that products get assigned to, e.g. "Standard", "Food", "Zero-rated"). Call get_taxes FIRST — a second group with the same meaning splits the catalogue and is a common way to end up charging two different taxes for one thing. The group charges nothing until you add rates with create_tax_rate or add_tax_rate_to_group, and no product uses it until someone assigns it. isStandard marks the company default — set it only if the merchant explicitly says so. CONFIRM the name with the merchant before calling.

name.description: What the merchant calls it, e.g. "Standard Tax"

isStandard.description: Make this the company default group. Default false

tools.name: hub_create_tax_rate
tools.title: Create tax rate
tools.description: Create a named tax rate ("State Sales Tax", "GST") with its percentage, and optionally put it straight into a tax group. Check get_taxes first: if a rate with this meaning already exists, add_tax_rate_to_group reuses it, which is almost always what the merchant wants — duplicating a rate means the next change has to be made twice and one of them gets forgotten. Give either percentage (the same at every outlet) or perOutlet (different per store) — never both, and never neither, since a rate with no percentage charges nothing. Without taxGroupId the rate exists but is charged nowhere. CONFIRM THE EXACT PERCENTAGE WITH THE MERCHANT before calling — do not infer it from suggest_tax_rate or from what is usual in that region. Sales already rung up are NOT recalculated — this only affects sales from now on.

name.description: What appears on the receipt, e.g. "GST", "State Sales Tax"

percentage.description: One percentage for every outlet, e.g. 13 for 13%

perOutlet.description: Outlet-specific percentages, using outlet ids from get_taxes. REPLACES the stored list whole — an outlet you leave out stops charging this rate

percentage.description: Percent as the merchant says it: 13 means 13%. Not a fraction — 0.13 would mean 0.13%

taxGroupId.description: Tax group id from get_taxes to add it to right away

compounding.description: Only with taxGroupId: charge on the running total including the rates above it. Default false

tools.name: hub_create_user
tools.title: Create POS user
tools.description: Add a POS user — someone who signs in at the till with a PIN. Mirrors the cabinet’s "New POS user" form: first and last name, a 4-6 digit PIN, a role, optionally a phone. They get access to every outlet of the company, which update_user can narrow afterwards. BACK-OFFICE (Hub) users are NOT created here: those are invited by email from the cabinet, and that invitation flow is not available through this tool. If the merchant wants someone who can log in to the back office, say that and point them at Manage → Team → Users → Add User. The role decides what the new person may do, so PERMISSIONS ARE POWER. Confirm with the merchant first, naming the person and the role out loud ("give Maria the Manager role — yes?"), and never act on a role change you inferred rather than were asked for. The change is live on the next request: rights are re-read from the role every time, so no one logs out and no agent key stops working — including yours, if the change reaches your own account. A new user also counts against the company plan’s user allowance and the call is refused once it is used up.

pincode.description: Required — 4 to 6 digits, what they type at the till

roleId.description: Role id from get_roles — required, and it decides their permissions

phone.description: Phone as the merchant said it, e.g. "+1 555 123 4567"

tools.name: hub_delete_category
tools.title: Delete category
tools.description: Delete a category. Takes the category id ONLY — look it up with get_categories and never guess. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT BEFORE CALLING, naming the category: there is no undo from here. Products in the category are NOT deleted — they are kept and simply lose this category, so a product that had no other category ends up uncategorised. A category that still has subcategories is refused: move or delete those first. So is a category synced from an integration.

categoryId.description: Category id from get_categories — not a name

tools.name: hub_delete_customer
tools.title: Delete customer
tools.description: Remove a customer from the merchant's list. Takes the customer ID ONLY — look it up with get_customers and never guess. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT BEFORE CALLING, naming the customer: there is no undo from here. Their past orders are kept. If several customers match, list them and ask which one instead of picking.

customerId.description: Customer id from get_customers — not a name

tools.name: hub_delete_media_file
tools.title: Delete media file
tools.description: Permanently delete one file from the media library. Takes the file ID from get_media_library ONLY — never guess it. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT BEFORE CALLING, naming the file: the image is destroyed and there is NO UNDO. Tell them this too, because the platform does not check it and nothing is cleaned up afterwards: if any product or category uses this image, it KEEPS the dead URL and its picture turns into a broken image — the file is not detached, it is only made unreachable. There is no reverse lookup here from a file to the products using it, so if they are unsure, say so and let them check on the Media screen in the cabinet rather than deleting on a guess. The file may also stay listed on that screen afterwards, because that screen is fed by a separate service. Removing a photo from ONE product without destroying the file is not this tool — that is a product edit.

fileId.description: File id from get_media_library — not a name or a URL

tools.name: hub_delete_modifier
tools.title: Delete modifier
tools.description: Remove a modifier from the catalogue AND detach it from every category at once — the till stops asking it everywhere. Check get_modifier first and tell the merchant which categories lose it. To stop asking it in ONE place only, use unlink_modifier_from_category. Past orders keep the options that were already rung up.

tools.name: hub_delete_modifier_choice
tools.title: Delete a choice
tools.description: Remove one choice from a modifier. Refused when it would leave a category asking for more choices than remain — the explanation names the category.

tools.name: hub_delete_outlet
tools.title: Delete outlet
tools.description: Close a point of sale permanently. Takes the outlet id from get_outlets. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT FIRST, naming the outlet — there is NO undo from here. Tell them what goes with it: the stock recorded AT that outlet is removed and is NOT moved anywhere else (transfer it out first if they want to keep it), and so are the outlet’s tax rate values and its per-outlet product visibility. Past orders, sessions and reports still name the outlet and are not touched, and the stations that belonged to it are NOT deleted — they have to be dealt with separately. An outlet that WooCommerce uses as its default is refused: the merchant must change that default or uninstall the WooCommerce extension first.

outletId.description: Outlet id from get_outlets — not a name

tools.name: hub_delete_product
tools.title: Delete product
tools.description: Remove a product from the merchant's catalogue. Takes the product ID ONLY — look it up with get_products and never guess. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT BEFORE CALLING, naming the product: this also removes all of its variants and there is no undo. If several products match, list them and ask which one instead of picking.

productId.description: Product id from get_products — not a name

tools.name: hub_delete_role
tools.title: Delete role
tools.description: Delete a role the merchant no longer uses. Takes the roleId from get_roles. CONFIRM FIRST, naming the role — there is no undo. A role that anyone still holds cannot be deleted: the server refuses and tells you how many people are on it. Move them with assign_role first, and check with the merchant which role they should land on — that move changes what those people can do. You cannot delete the role you are signed in under.

roleId.description: Role id from get_roles — not a role name

tools.name: hub_delete_station
tools.title: Delete till
tools.description: Remove a till from Run → Stations. Takes the station id from get_stations. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT FIRST, naming the station — there is NO undo from here, and it takes a working register out of service: the device that used it has to be set up again in the POS app, and it comes back as a NEW station with a new id. A station reporting IN_USE is REFUSED, exactly as the cabinet greys the button out — the shift has to be closed on the device first. If the merchant insists that till is idle, the flag is stale (it was closed while the device was offline); it clears once the device reconnects, so try again then instead of forcing anything. Past orders, sessions and End of Session reports keep naming this station and are not touched.

stationId.description: Station id from get_stations — not a name

tools.name: hub_delete_supplier
tools.title: Delete supplier
tools.description: Remove a supplier the merchant no longer buys from. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT FIRST, naming the supplier — there is no undo from here. Its item links go with it, so any auto-reorder rule pointing at this supplier stops producing suggestions. REFUSED while the supplier still has an open purchase order (anything not fully received): receive or cancel those first — get_purchase_orders filtered by this supplier shows them. Purchase orders already placed are kept and still name the supplier.

supplierId.description: Supplier id from get_suppliers — not a name

tools.name: hub_delete_tax_group
tools.title: Delete tax group
tools.description: Delete a tax group. Takes the tax group id from get_taxes. THIS MOVES PRODUCTS: every product assigned to this group is re-pointed at replacementTaxGroupId, or — if you omit it — left with NO tax group at all, meaning those products are sold UNTAXED from that moment. Always ask the merchant which of the two they want and pass a replacement unless they say otherwise. The rates inside it are NOT deleted; they stay available to the other groups (use delete_tax_rate if the merchant really wants a rate gone). CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT BEFORE CALLING, naming the group and how many products it affects. There is no undo. Sales already rung up are NOT recalculated — this only affects sales from now on.

taxGroupId.description: Tax group id from get_taxes — not a name

replacementTaxGroupId.description: Tax group its products move to. OMIT ONLY if the merchant wants those products left untaxed

tools.name: hub_delete_tax_rate
tools.title: Delete tax rate
tools.description: Permanently delete a tax rate FROM THE WHOLE COMPANY. Takes the tax rate id from get_taxes. THIS CASCADES: the rate is stripped out of every tax group that lists it and all of its per-outlet percentages are deleted with it. Products in those groups immediately stop being charged this tax. This is almost never what a merchant means when they say "remove the tax from X" — that is remove_tax_rate_from_group. Use this one only when they say the rate should not exist at all any more. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT BEFORE CALLING, naming the rate and listing every group it will disappear from. There is no undo and no way to recover the percentages. Sales already rung up are NOT recalculated — this only affects sales from now on.

taxRateId.description: Tax rate id from get_taxes — not a name

tools.name: hub_export_records
tools.title: Export records
tools.description: Dump one resource in spreadsheet shape — every record flattened to the same columns the import tools accept, WITH its id. Answers 'export my catalogue / my customers', and it is the required first step before any import that changes existing records: the `updates` arrays all key on the ids this returns. For QUESTIONS about the data ("how many products", "find John") use get_products / get_customers / get_categories / get_outlets / get_options instead — they read better and filter server-side. LIMITATIONS: no filtering and no sorting; records come back in stored order, one window at a time. It also cannot produce a FILE — if the merchant wants a .csv/.xlsx download, send them to Settings → Import / Export → Export in the cabinet and do not page through thousands of rows to imitate it. Money is in minor units (cents), matching what the import tools read back.

resource.description: Which resource to dump. "options" means product attributes (Size, Colour) — the cabinet calls them Attributes

tools.name: hub_export_stock_csv
tools.title: Export stock CSV
tools.description: The stock export file for ONE outlet, as CSV text: Variation ID, Product Name, Variation name, SKU, Stock Management, Cur Qty, New Qty. Use it when the merchant asks for the stock sheet itself — a stocktake worksheet, a hand-off to a supplier, 'give me my stock as CSV'. For stock QUESTIONS — how many of X are left, what is running out, history of a change — use get_stock, find_low_stock and get_stock_history: they filter on the server and explain when tracking is switched off. This dump includes untracked rows and cannot tell "zero" apart from "not counted here". It is READ-ONLY: to write counts back, edit the New Qty column and send the file to import_stock_csv. Large catalogues are truncated — the reply reports the true row count.

outletId.description: Outlet id from get_outlets — not a store name

maxRows.description: Data rows to return, default 200, max 2000

tools.name: hub_find_low_stock
tools.title: Low stock
tools.description: What is running out. Answers 'what is low', 'what do I need to reorder', 'what has run out at the warehouse'. Returns the stock-tracked (variant, outlet) lines at or below a threshold, lowest first. Threshold defaults to 5; pass threshold: 0 for "what has actually hit zero". Lines where stock is NOT tracked are excluded on purpose — they have no count, so they can never be low, and reporting them would invent a shortage that does not exist. This is per outlet: the same variant can be empty in one shop and full in another. For one specific product use get_stock instead.

outletId.description: Outlet id from get_outlets. Omit to cover every outlet

threshold.description: Report lines with this many units or fewer. Default 5; use 0 for out-of-stock only

limit.description: How many lines to return, default 25

tools.name: hub_get_booking_availability
tools.title: Check booking availability
tools.description: The bookable windows for a product over a date range, per resource, with what is already taken. Quote times from THIS — never compute a grid yourself: the engine applies the hours, the buffer, notice and advance limits, and the outlet timezone, and a hold whose start is not exactly a slot start is refused. Ask for a few days at a time; a year-wide range is slow and pointless.

from.description: ISO instant, start of the range, e.g. "2026-09-12T00:00:00Z"

to.description: ISO instant, end of the range

outletId.description: The shop the booking is for — decides the local wall clock. Omit for the company default

tools.name: hub_get_booking_events
tools.title: Read booking history
tools.description: The trail of what happened to bookings — held, confirmed, cancelled, expired — newest first, with who did it. Use it to answer "what happened to this booking"; an actor of `system` is the server freeing an expired hold, not a person. Each row is immutable, so this is the record even when the booking itself is gone.

productId.description: Narrow to one product. Omit for the whole company

limit.description: How many rows, newest first. Default 100

tools.name: hub_get_booking_resources
tools.title: List booking resources
tools.description: List what can be booked — the staff, rooms, tables or assets in the company directory. A resource is whatever can only be in one place at a time, and it is shared across services: the same barber is one resource whether he cuts hair or trims a beard, which is why booking him for one closes the other. Read this before creating anything and reuse what is there.

tools.name: hub_get_booking_rules
tools.title: List booking rule sets
tools.description: List the reusable booking policies the merchant already has — opening hours, slot length, buffer, how far ahead people may book. A rule set is shared by every product pointing at it, exactly like a tax table, so ALWAYS read this before creating one and offer an existing set when it fits. Editing a set changes every product that uses it.

tools.name: hub_get_categories
tools.title: List categories
tools.description: The merchant's product categories, as the tree they see in the cabinet: every category with its subcategories nested inside it, sorted by sortOrder. Answers "what categories do I have", "is there a Drinks category", "where does Beer sit". Use it to get the category id any other tool needs. It returns categories ONLY — never products, and never a product count. There is no way to list the products of a category from this server today: get_products searches by name or SKU and cannot filter by category, so say that plainly instead of guessing. To put a product INTO a category, go to the product side: create_product / update_product take categoryIds. The whole tree comes back at once — there is no paging and no search argument, so filter by name yourself.

tools.name: hub_get_category_modifiers
tools.title: List modifier placements
tools.description: Where modifiers are actually asked: one row per category↔modifier link, with that category’s own rules (required, min, max, order). This is what makes a modifier reach the till, so use it to answer "what options does this category ask" or "where is this modifier used". Narrow to one category with categoryId. Remember products also inherit their ancestors’ links, so a subcategory asks more than its own rows show. The id on each row is the LINK id — that is what update_category_modifier and unlink_modifier_from_category take.

categoryId.description: Category id from get_categories. Omit for every category

tools.name: hub_get_customer
tools.title: Get customer details
tools.description: Everything known about ONE customer: addresses, notes, how many orders they placed, what they spent and what was refunded. Takes the customer ID from get_customers, never a name. Use it before answering a question about a specific person — the list leaves notes and refunds out.

customerId.description: Customer id from get_customers — not a name

tools.name: hub_get_customer_orders
tools.title: Customer order history
tools.description: ONE customer's history as a single timeline, newest first: their orders AND the refunds taken against them, each row marked type "order" or "refund" — the same list the customer screen shows. Answers 'what has this person bought', 'did we refund them', 'when were they last in'. Takes the customer ID from get_customers, never a name. get_orders with customerIds returns the orders alone and a total count; use this tool when the refunds belong in the answer. No total count comes back here — keep paging until a page returns fewer rows than asked for.

customerId.description: Customer id from get_customers — not a name

tools.name: hub_get_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List the merchant's customers. Answers 'who are my customers', 'find John's email', 'has this person bought from us'. Search matches email, first name, last name and full name — NOT phone numbers, addresses or notes. LIMITATION — there is no sorting: results come back in stored order and cannot be ordered by spend, name or last visit. So 'my best customers' or 'who spent the most' CANNOT be answered from this tool, and you must NOT page through everyone trying. Say plainly that sorting is not supported yet, then offer what does work: search by a name or email, or ask the merchant to narrow it down.

search.description: Filter by email, first name, last name or full name

tools.name: hub_get_employee_orders
tools.title: Employee orders
