tools.description: The orders ONE staff member rang up in a date range. Takes the employee id from get_employee_sales, never a name. Use it to back up a claim about a person — 'show me the sales behind Maria's number', 'which orders did he refund'.

employeeId.description: Employee id from get_employee_sales — not a name

endDate.description: End of the window, ISO 8601. Inclusive of the day when a bare date is given

outlets.description: Outlet ids to restrict to. Omit for all outlets

stations.description: Station ids to restrict to. Omit for all stations

tools.name: hub_get_employee_sales
tools.title: Employee sales
tools.description: Sales per staff member for a date range — Reports → Employee Sales. Answers 'who is my best seller', 'how much did Maria sell', 'who took the most refunds', 'average ticket per employee'. One row per employee with orders, gross sales, refunds, tips and average transaction. Staff lists are short, so ranking is safe: pull the rows and sort them yourself rather than asking the merchant to narrow down. Pass employeeId to get a single person. For the actual orders one person rang up, use get_employee_orders.

endDate.description: End of the window, ISO 8601. Inclusive of the day when a bare date is given

outlets.description: Outlet ids to restrict to. Omit for all outlets

stations.description: Station ids to restrict to. Omit for all stations

employeeId.description: Restrict to one employee, by id from a previous call

tools.name: hub_get_extension_catalog
tools.title: Browse extension catalog
tools.description: The extension STORE: every built-in extension the platform offers, the same list for every merchant. Answers 'what can I add', 'do you have a WooCommerce integration', 'can I get X'. For 'what do I already have', use get_installed_extensions instead — this tool only flags each entry with `installed`. `availableOnYourPlan: false` means the subscription plan excludes it: the store hides it in the cabinet and install_extension will refuse — say so instead of trying. LIMITATIONS, do not paper over them: the platform stores only a name, a category, a price and an id per built-in extension — there is NO stored description, so do not invent what an extension does; say what the name and category say and offer to open its page in the cabinet. `price` is a bare stored string with no currency attached — quote it verbatim, never as a formatted amount. Custom extensions built by an organisation are NOT in this list (they need an organisation scope this agent key does not carry); they do show up in get_installed_extensions once installed.

tools.name: hub_get_extension_surfaces
tools.title: List extension screens
tools.description: What the installed extensions ADD to the apps — the answer to "where did this new menu item come from", "what is this extra block on the product page", "what did installing X actually change". Every entry belongs to an installed extension; nothing here is part of the base product. Read `platform` to know where it shows up: `hub` = this admin cabinet, `builder` = the POS flow builder, `render` = the station screen. Within `hub`, type `merchant-hub-page` is a navigation entry of its own and `merchant-hub-widget` is a block embedded in a detail page — `attachedTo` says which one (products / orders / customers / users). LIMITATION: this tells you which extension-provided screens EXIST, not what they contain — each one is an embedded page owned by its extension, and this agent cannot open or read it. It also cannot say which extension contributed a given entry. To go the other way — what is installed at all — use get_installed_extensions.

tools.name: hub_get_financial_summary
tools.title: Financial summary
tools.description: THE headline money report for a date range — the same numbers as Reports → Financial Summary. Answers 'how much did we make last week', 'what were sales this month', 'how much tax do I owe', 'what lands in my bank'. Returns gross sales, discounts, refunds, fees, tax, tips, net sales, and the settlement split (card / cash / custom) down to what the merchant actually receives. Start here for any "how did the business do" question, and only reach for get_sales_breakdown when the merchant wants the individual orders behind these totals.

endDate.description: End of the window, ISO 8601. Inclusive of the day when a bare date is given

outlets.description: Outlet ids to restrict to. Omit for all outlets

stations.description: Station ids to restrict to. Omit for all stations

tools.name: hub_get_installed_extensions
tools.title: List installed extensions
tools.description: What THIS company actually has installed — built-in and organisation-built (custom) extensions alike. This is the answer to 'which extensions do I have', 'is WooCommerce turned on for me', 'what am I paying for'. Not to be confused with get_extension_catalog, which lists what exists on the platform whether or not this merchant has it. Each row carries `extensionId` (pass this to install_extension / uninstall_extension) and `companyExtensionId` (the install record itself — you never need to pass that one). `description` is filled in only for custom extensions; built-in ones store no prose, so do not guess what they do. LIMITATION: the install date is not stored — you cannot say when an extension was added or who added it. To answer what an installed extension CHANGED in the cabinet — a new menu entry, a block on a detail page — use get_extension_surfaces.

tools.name: hub_get_linkable_items
tools.title: List items a supplier could carry
tools.description: Catalogue items this supplier does NOT carry yet but could — the picker behind "add items to supplier". Feed what you choose to link_supplier_items. Only stock-managed items appear: something the merchant does not track stock for cannot be purchase-ordered at all, so if an expected item is missing here and missing from get_supplier_items too, the reason is almost always that stock tracking is off for it — say that instead of guessing. Omit supplierId to search the whole linkable catalogue, e.g. while deciding which supplier to create. Returns everything matching, unpaged, so pass a search.

supplierId.description: Supplier id — omit to see the whole linkable catalogue

search.description: Match product name, item name, SKU or barcode

tools.name: hub_get_media_library
tools.title: List media files
tools.description: List the image files stored on the merchant's account. Answers 'what images do I have', 'do I already have a photo of X', 'what did I upload recently', and it is where you get a file id before deleting one, or a URL to reuse on a product or category. Newest first; search is a case-insensitive match on the FILE NAME only. LIMITATIONS, state them rather than working around them: there is no other sorting, and no title, alt text, description, folder, file size or image dimensions here — the Media screen in the cabinet shows those, but they are stored by a different service that this tool cannot read, so it may list files this tool does not and vice versa. There is also NO WAY TO RENAME a file from here: if the merchant asks to rename one, or to change its alt text, title or folder, say that has to be done on the Media screen in the cabinet. Do not delete and re-upload to fake a rename.

search.description: Filter by file name, e.g. "logo" or "shirt"

tools.name: hub_get_modifier
tools.title: Get modifier
tools.description: One modifier in full: its choices with prices and defaults, and every category it is linked to with that category’s own rules. Read this before editing — update_modifier REPLACES the whole choice list, so you need the current one to send back. Each choice carries price (formatted, for reading out) and priceAmount (plain, what the write tools accept back). Pass priceAmount, never price.

tools.name: hub_get_modifiers
tools.title: List modifiers
tools.description: Every modifier the merchant has — the questions the till can ask about an item, with their choices and prices. Start here for anything about options, add-ons, extras, toppings, sizes, milk, cooking temperature or "how do I let them choose X". Each row says how it is answered: "Pick one" (radio), "Pick many" (checkboxes), "Pick many · qty" or "stepper per choice" (the last two count UNITS, so one choice taken three times counts as 3). usedIn is how many categories it is linked to — a modifier with usedIn 0 is invisible at the till no matter how well it is set up.

tools.name: hub_get_order
tools.title: Get order details
tools.description: Everything inside ONE order: line items with quantity, unit price and per-line tax, custom sales, gift-card and other non-revenue lines, the totals block, every payment taken (method, processor, card type and last 4, tip, change), every refund already made against it, plus the customer, outlet, station, employee and order notes. Answers 'what was in order 1042', 'how did they pay', 'was this one refunded', 'why is this total different'. Takes the order ID from get_orders — a receipt number will NOT work, search for it with get_orders first. READ-ONLY, and there is no sibling tool that writes: an order's status cannot be changed, an order cannot be cancelled or completed, and a refund cannot be created from this API — refunds are taken on the POS terminal against the original payment. Say that plainly instead of hunting for another tool.

orderId.description: Order id from get_orders — not a receipt number

tools.name: hub_get_order_count
tools.title: Count orders
tools.description: How many orders the company has, in total or at given outlets — 'how many orders do we have', 'how busy is the King Street shop'. Cheap: it counts, it loads no order data. It counts EVERY order ever recorded and takes no date, status or source filter. For anything time-boxed or filtered, call get_orders and read its `matching` count, or use get_financial_summary for a period.

outlets.description: Outlet ids to restrict to. Omit to count every outlet

tools.name: hub_get_orders
tools.title: List orders
tools.description: Find orders — the same rows as Manage → Orders. Answers 'show me order 1042', 'what did we sell on Saturday', 'are there parked orders', 'orders rung up by Maria', 'orders over $500 at the King Street shop'. Filter by receipt number, status, source, employee, customer, product, date window, order total, outlet or station. Results are ALWAYS newest first — there is no other sorting, so a "biggest order" question needs the amount filter, not paging. Search matches the receipt number and the order id ONLY, never customer names or product names: for those, pass customerIds from get_customers or productIds from get_products. One row per order with its total; for what is INSIDE an order — line items, payments, refunds, notes — call get_order with the id from here. For how much the business took over a period use get_financial_summary or get_sales_breakdown instead of adding these rows up.

search.description: Receipt number or order id. Does NOT match customer or product names

status.description: Final POS statuses: "completed", "refunded", "partial-refund", "parked". WooCommerce orders keep their own ("processing", "on-hold", "pending", "cancelled", "failed") — pass "other" to match every status outside the four Final POS ones

employeeIds.description: Employee ids — from get_employee_sales, not names

customerIds.description: Customer ids from get_customers, not names

productIds.description: Product ids from get_products — matches orders containing them

startDate.description: Only orders created at or after this ISO 8601 moment

endDate.description: Only orders created at or before this ISO 8601 moment

minTotal.description: Minimum order total in MINOR units (cents), e.g. 50000 for $500

maxTotal.description: Maximum order total in MINOR units (cents)

outlets.description: Outlet ids. Combined with stations by OR

stations.description: Station ids. Combined with outlets by OR

tools.name: hub_get_outlets
tools.title: List outlets
tools.description: Every point of sale (store, location, branch) the merchant has — the same list as Settings → Outlets. Answers 'how many stores do I have', 'what is the address of the King Street shop', 'what is that location’s phone number'. ALSO THE WAY TO TURN A STORE NAME INTO AN ID: the reports, inventory and station tools filter by outlet ID and never by name, so when the merchant says 'sales for King Street' or 'stock at the warehouse', call this FIRST and pass the id you find here. Returns every outlet in one call — the list is short, there is no paging and no server-side search, so match the name yourself. Deleted outlets are not returned. Outlets carry NO opening hours, timezone or currency: store hours are not stored anywhere on this platform and currency is a company-wide setting, so say that plainly instead of guessing. Per-outlet tax percentages are not here either — those belong to the tax tools.

tools.name: hub_get_payment_methods_breakdown
tools.title: Payment methods breakdown
tools.description: How customers paid over a date range, netted of refunds — 'how much came in on card vs cash', 'what did processing fees cost me', 'how much hits my bank account'. Card and each custom processor also report their processing fees and the resulting deposit; cash has no fees. The same aggregation the Financial Summary settlement section uses, so the two always agree.

endDate.description: End of the window, ISO 8601. Inclusive of the day when a bare date is given

outlets.description: Outlet ids to restrict to. Omit for all outlets

stations.description: Station ids to restrict to. Omit for all stations

tools.name: hub_get_permissions
tools.title: List permissions
tools.description: The catalogue of permissions a role can be given — every switch on the Roles screen, with the id create_role and update_role need. Call this to turn a request like 'let her see the reports' into the right permission id; match on the label and the permission path, and ask the merchant if two of them could both be meant. Permissions are granted exactly as named — there is no parent-grants-the-children cascade here — so pass every line the merchant actually needs. The list is the same for every merchant; it is not their current setup. For what a role currently grants, use get_roles.

tools.name: hub_get_product_booking_setup
tools.title: Read a product booking setup
tools.description: Which resources serve this bookable product. Use it to check a product is actually ready to take bookings before quoting availability — an empty resource list means every hold will be refused, however correct the rule set looks.

productId.description: Product id from get_products — not a name

tools.name: hub_get_product_options
tools.title: List product options
tools.description: List the variation axes the merchant already has — e.g. 'Size' with Small/Medium/Large. Call this BEFORE creating a product with variants and offer the existing axes instead of inventing new ones. Only call create_product_option when the merchant needs an axis that is not in this list.

tools.name: hub_get_products
tools.title: List products
tools.description: List products in the merchant's catalogue. Answers 'what products do I have', 'find the Coca-Cola product', 'how much is X'. Pass categoryIds to answer 'what is in the Drinks category' — take the ids from get_categories, which does not return products itself. LIMITATION — there is no sorting: results come back in catalogue order and cannot be ordered by price, name or date. So 'the most expensive products' CANNOT be answered from this tool, and you must NOT page through the whole catalogue trying. Say plainly that sorting is not supported yet, then offer what does work: search by a name or SKU, filter by category, or ask the merchant to narrow it down.

search.description: Filter by product name or SKU (partial match)

The rules are per category, so the same modifier can be required here and optional elsewhere. required means the cashier cannot finish the line until they answer. min/max count distinct choices, or UNITS when the modifier uses quantities. Refused when the category already inherits this modifier from a parent category (link it to the parent or the child, not both), when it is already linked, and when the rules could not be satisfied — for example asking for at least 3 when only 2 choices are sold at every outlet. Linking a modifier to a PARENT category detaches it from any subcategories that already had it, since they now inherit it.

required.description: The cashier must answer before ringing up. Default false

min.description: Fewest that must be chosen. Setting this makes it required

max.description: Most that may be chosen. Omit for no cap

sortOrder.description: Position among this category’s modifiers. Omit to append

tools.name: hub_link_supplier_items
tools.title: Link, re-price or unlink supplier items
tools.description: Change what a supplier carries and what it charges, in one call: `add` new items, `update` the cost or part number of items already linked, `remove` items it no longer sells. variantId comes from get_linkable_items for `add` and from get_supplier_items for `update` / `remove`. unitCost is what the merchant PAYS per unit, as a human amount like "12.50" in the company currency — never the selling price, and never cents. It is only the DEFAULT that prefills new order lines: changing it does not re-price purchase orders already placed. Adding an item that is already linked is refused, so read the current list first rather than re-adding blindly. REMOVING is the destructive half — confirm it with the merchant, and tell them it also EDITS ORDERS THAT ARE ALREADY WRITTEN: the item’s line is dropped from every suggested and draft order from this supplier, which changes their totals. Orders already sent keep their lines, the item stays in the catalogue, but it can no longer be added to a new order from this supplier, and any auto-reorder rule pointing at this supplier for it stops producing suggestions.

supplierId.description: Supplier id from get_suppliers — not a name

add.description: Items to start buying from this supplier

unitCost.description: Cost the merchant pays, e.g. "12.50". Stored as 0 if omitted

partNumber.description: The supplier’s own code for this item

update.description: Already-linked items to re-price or re-code

remove.description: Item ids from get_supplier_items to stop buying from this supplier

tools.name: hub_receive_purchase_order
tools.title: Receive a delivery
tools.description: Book a delivery in against an order that was sent: ADDS THE RECEIVED QUANTITIES TO REAL STOCK at the order’s outlet and updates the item cost book. This is not a note — it changes inventory. CONFIRM THE QUANTITIES WITH THE MERCHANT FIRST, item by item, and record what genuinely ARRIVED, not what was ordered — they differ, which is the whole point of receiving. Only `sent` and `partially_received` orders can be received; each item must be one that was ordered; receiving more than ordered is allowed. A short delivery leaves the order `partially_received` — receive again when the rest turns up. A CALL THAT RETURNS IS NOT PROOF EVERY ITEM LANDED — check `partialFailure`, and `stockApplied.complete` on a large delivery. IF IT FAILS, DO NOT RETRY BLINDLY: "still being received" means a previous delivery is being applied right now (get_receive_progress), and a wrong-status error means it was already fully received. Call get_purchase_order to see what actually landed before deciding anything. unitCost is what this delivery actually cost per unit — pass the invoice price if it differs from the order. When it does differ, the supplier’s stored cost is NOT updated unless you list that item in updateSupplierCostVariantIds, so ask the merchant whether the new price is the going rate or a one-off.

purchaseOrderId.description: Purchase order id from get_purchase_orders — not a PO number

variantId.description: Item id from get_supplier_items — the supplier must carry it

quantity.description: How many, in the unit the item is sold in. May be fractional for goods sold by weight or length

unitCost.description: Cost per unit the merchant pays, e.g. "12.50". Never cents, never the selling price

discount.description: Flat discount on this line, e.g. "2.00". Not with discountPercent

discountPercent.description: Discount as a percentage of this line’s goods

feePerUnit.description: Extra cost per unit on this line

invoiceNumber.description: Supplier invoice number for this delivery

receivedAt.description: ISO date the goods arrived — defaults to now

updateSupplierCostVariantIds.description: Items whose new unitCost should become the supplier’s stored cost from now on

discount.description: Flat discount on the whole order, e.g. "25.00". Not with discountPercent

discountPercent.description: Discount as a percentage of the items subtotal

shippingFee.description: Shipping charged on the order, e.g. "18.00"

dutyFees.description: Duty / customs charged on the order

customFees.description: Any other named charge on the order, e.g. "Handling"

tools.name: hub_receive_stock_transfer
tools.title: Receive stock transfer
tools.description: Confirm that a transfer arrived: the destination outlet gains the units and the transfer closes. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT FIRST — this adds stock and cannot be undone from here. Only do it when they say the goods are physically there; confirming a transfer that never arrived hides a loss instead of recording one. Takes stockTransferId (from get_stock_transfer), NOT the transactionId. Only applies to a receive-transfer leg still in-transit; a transfer already completed has nothing left to receive.

tools.name: hub_record_received_goods
tools.title: Record goods received with no order
tools.description: Stock that arrived with no purchase order behind it — the merchant bought it on the spot, or it was ordered outside the platform. Creates the order already fully received and ADDS THE QUANTITIES TO REAL STOCK at the outlet, in one step. Use this ONLY when no order exists. If the goods match an order that was sent, use receive_purchase_order instead — otherwise the same delivery is counted twice, once here and once when someone receives the real order. Check get_purchase_orders for an open order from this supplier before calling. The items must already be linked to the supplier (get_supplier_items) and stock-managed at the outlet. There is no undo: correcting a mistake means a stock adjustment afterwards.

tools.name: hub_remove_reorder_rule
tools.title: Turn off auto-reorder for an item
tools.description: Stop watching one item: it will no longer be suggested for reordering however low it runs. Its thresholds are forgotten, so turning it back on means setting them again. Suggestions already produced for this item are not withdrawn — cancel those orders separately if the merchant wants them gone.

tools.name: hub_remove_tax_rate_from_group
tools.title: Remove rate from group
tools.description: Stop ONE tax group charging a rate. The rate itself, its percentages and its use by other groups are untouched — this only drops the link. This is what the merchant means by "remove the city tax from Food". Use delete_tax_rate ONLY when they want the rate gone from the whole company. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT: every product in this group immediately stops being charged this tax. Sales already rung up are NOT recalculated — this only affects sales from now on.

tools.name: hub_remove_user
tools.title: Remove team member
tools.description: Remove someone from the merchant's team — the tool for 'she left', 'take the leaver off'. Takes the userId from get_team ONLY, never a name. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT BEFORE CALLING, naming the person: there is no undo from here. If two people share a name, list them and ask which. They stop being able to sign in immediately; their past orders and sales figures are kept, so reports about them still work. You cannot remove the account this agent key belongs to — the server refuses, so that an administrator cannot lock themselves out.

userId.description: User id from get_team — not a name

tools.name: hub_rename_station
tools.title: Rename till
tools.description: Rename one station. Takes the station id from get_stations. Renaming is safe and takes effect everywhere — past orders, sessions and reports store the id and look the name up. The name is the ONLY thing the cabinet lets anyone change on an existing station, and the only thing this tool changes. A station cannot be moved to another outlet, and its device, card reader and POS layout are not editable from here — moving a till to another store means creating a new station there and deleting this one, which loses its id.

stationId.description: Station id from get_stations — not a name

name.description: The new station name

tools.name: hub_reorder_categories
tools.title: Reorder categories
tools.description: Set the display order of several categories in one call — "put Drinks first", "sort my categories alphabetically". Lowest sortOrder shows first, and ordering only applies among categories that share the same parent. Send every category whose position should change, with the ids from get_categories; ones you leave out keep their current order, which can leave two categories tied. It changes NOTHING but the order — for a rename or a move use update_category.

sortOrder.description: Position among its siblings, lowest first

tools.name: hub_reorder_category_modifiers
tools.title: Reorder a category’s modifiers
tools.description: Set the order the till asks a category’s modifiers in. Pass EVERY link id for that category exactly once, in the order wanted — a partial list is refused. Read them from get_category_modifiers with that categoryId.

orderedIds.description: Every link id for this category, each once, in ask order

tools.name: hub_reorder_modifier_choices
tools.title: Reorder choices
tools.description: Set the order the choices appear in at the till. Pass EVERY current choice id exactly once, in the order wanted — a partial list is refused. Read them from get_modifier first.

orderedChoiceIds.description: Every current choice id, each exactly once, in display order

tools.name: hub_send_purchase_order
tools.title: Send purchase order to supplier
tools.description: Place the order: moves a `draft` or `suggested` order to `sent` and, when asked, EMAILS IT TO THE SUPPLIER. ASK THE MERCHANT WHETHER TO EMAIL, EVERY TIME, and only then pass sendEmail: true — that message leaves the platform and cannot be recalled. Default is false, which records the order as placed without mailing anything: the right choice when they ordered by phone, in person, or through the supplier’s own portal. Emailing needs a contactEmail on the supplier; without one, send with sendEmail: false and tell them why. The email carries the order in its body — this tool cannot attach the PO PDF the cabinet produces. After sending, the order can no longer be edited; only receiving or cancelling remain.

purchaseOrderId.description: Purchase order id from get_purchase_orders — not a PO number

sendEmail.description: Email the supplier. Defaults to false — set true ONLY after the merchant said to send it

tools.name: hub_set_product_booking_setup
tools.title: Make a product bookable
tools.description: Point a booking product at its rule set AND the resources that serve it — both in one call, because a product with only one of them takes no bookings at all. `resourceIds` REPLACES the current list rather than adding to it, so pass every resource that should serve the product. The product must already exist and be of the booking type (create_product with productType "booking").

resourceIds.description: Every resource that can serve this product, ids from get_booking_resources

tools.name: hub_set_reorder_rule
tools.title: Turn on auto-reorder for an item
tools.description: Tell the platform to watch one item and suggest reordering it when stock runs low: below lowStockPoint, suggest ordering reorderQuantity from this supplier. Calling it again on the same item replaces the rule rather than adding a second one. The supplier MUST already carry this item (get_supplier_items) — otherwise the rule would draft orders to a supplier that cannot fulfil them, and it is refused. The thresholds apply company-wide unless you pass outletOverrides, which set a different point or quantity per outlet — a busy store may need a higher one than a quiet one. This only produces SUGGESTIONS. Nothing is ever ordered or emailed automatically.

supplierId.description: Supplier to reorder from — must already carry this item

lowStockPoint.description: Suggest reordering once stock falls below this

outletOverrides.description: Per-outlet thresholds for outlets that differ from the default

lowStockPoint.description: Omit to inherit the company-wide point

reorderQuantity.description: Omit to inherit the company-wide quantity

tools.name: hub_suggest_tax_rate
tools.title: Suggest tax rate
tools.description: Look up the statutory headline rate for a country (and US state / Canadian province). Answers 'what should I charge in Ontario', 'what is the VAT in Germany'. This is a reference lookup — it changes NOTHING and creates nothing; use create_tax_rate to actually charge it. Report the `confidence` and any `note` back to the merchant verbatim: local / city taxes are not included and the merchant, not you, decides the real rate.

state.description: US state or Canadian province code, e.g. "NY", "ON". Needed for US and CA

tools.name: hub_sync_order_to_ecommerce
tools.title: Sync order to store
tools.description: Push one order to the company's connected online store (WooCommerce): creates it there the first time, updates it afterwards, and syncs its notes. Use ONLY when the merchant says an order is missing from or stale in their online store — 'this sale never showed up in WooCommerce'. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT BEFORE CALLING, naming the order: it writes into their live store and nothing here can undo it. It changes NOTHING in Final POS — it is not a way to change status, cancel an order or refund anything. Companies with no supported platform connected get a no-op.

orderId.description: Order id from get_orders — not a receipt number

tools.name: hub_sync_refund_to_ecommerce
tools.title: Sync refund to store
tools.description: Push a refund that ALREADY exists in Final POS to the connected WooCommerce store, so the online order shows as refunded there. Takes the REFUND id from get_refunds — the order id will not work. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT BEFORE CALLING: it creates a refund on their live store, there is no undo from here, and calling it twice creates a second refund there. It does NOT move money back to the customer and it does NOT create a refund in Final POS — that happens on the POS terminal.

refundId.description: Refund id from get_refunds — not an order id

tools.name: hub_uninstall_extension
tools.title: Uninstall extension
tools.description: Uninstall an extension from the company. Takes the `extensionId` from get_installed_extensions, never a name. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT BEFORE CALLING, naming the extension: the install record is deleted for good — there is NO undo from here, and re-installing does not bring the extension’s own settings back. It also removes what the extension added to the cabinet (its menu entries and detail-page blocks disappear for every user) and runs the extension’s own teardown: WooCommerce stops syncing the store, Vendara and Zapier are disabled, TIMEmSYSTEM’s settings are deleted, Custom Payment queues a final invoice for the transactions already processed. Orders, products and customers that came in through the extension are NOT deleted. If the merchant only wants to stop using it for a while, tell them there is no pause — uninstall is the only option.

extensionId.description: extensionId from get_installed_extensions — not a name

tools.name: hub_unlink_modifier_from_category
tools.title: Stop asking a modifier on a category
tools.description: Stop asking a modifier in one category. The modifier itself survives and keeps working everywhere else — use delete_modifier to remove it entirely. Takes the LINK id from get_category_modifiers, not the modifier id. If the category inherits the same modifier from a parent, the till keeps asking it; unlink it from the parent instead.

categoryModifierId.description: Link id from get_category_modifiers — the link, NOT the modifier and NOT the category

tools.name: hub_update_category
tools.title: Update category
tools.description: Rename a category, change its description or image, move it under a different parent, or set its sortOrder. Takes the category id from get_categories, never a name. Only the fields you pass are changed. parentId can only MOVE the category under another one; making an existing subcategory top-level again is not supported here, and neither is it in the cabinet. A category synced from an integration (WooCommerce and the like) is read-only and will be refused — it has to be changed in that platform. This never touches which products are in the category; that lives on the product (update_product, categoryIds).

categoryId.description: Category id from get_categories — not a name

parentId.description: New parent id from get_categories. Cannot be the category itself or one of its own subcategories

sortOrder.description: Position among its siblings, lowest first

tools.name: hub_update_category_modifier
tools.title: Change a modifier’s rules on a category
tools.description: Change how a modifier is asked in ONE category — required, min, max, order — leaving every other category alone. Omit a field to leave it as it is; pass null to min or max to CLEAR that limit. The two are different, so be deliberate. The platform tidies the combination and reports what it actually stored: turning required on sets a minimum of 1, any minimum of 1 or more turns required on, and a "Pick one" modifier keeps no min or max at all. Read the result rather than assuming your input was kept. required: false together with a minimum of 1 or more is a contradiction and is refused.

categoryModifierId.description: Link id from get_category_modifiers — the link, NOT the modifier and NOT the category

tools.name: hub_update_customer
tools.title: Update customer
tools.description: Change contact details on an existing customer. Takes the customer ID from get_customers, never a name. Only the fields you pass are changed, but an address you pass REPLACES the stored one whole — read it back with get_customer first and resend the parts that should stay. Notes are not editable here: use add_customer_note.

customerId.description: Customer id from get_customers — not a name

tools.name: hub_update_modifier
tools.title: Edit modifier
tools.description: Rename a modifier and/or REPLACE its whole choice list. Passing choices is a full replacement: whatever you send becomes the list and anything you leave out is DELETED. Read get_modifier first and send the complete set back, keeping each choice’s id so prices and till history stay attached. To change one choice, use update_modifier_choice instead — it is safer and cannot drop the others. selectionType and allowQuantity cannot be changed; a modifier that needs a different kind of answer has to be created fresh. Renaming alone never breaks a rule; replacing choices can, and is refused with an explanation if it would.

name.description: New name. Must stay unique for the merchant, ignoring case

choices.description: The COMPLETE new choice list. Omitting this leaves the choices untouched

choiceId.description: Keep an existing choice by its id

name.description: What the cashier sees, e.g. "Oat milk"

price.description: Extra charge per unit, e.g. "0.70". Omit or "0" for a choice that costs nothing

isDefault.description: Pre-selected at the till. On "Pick one" at most one choice may have it

sortOrder.description: Position in the list. Omit to append

unavailableOutletIds.description: Outlets where this choice is NOT sold (an exception list — omit or [] means sold everywhere). Outlet ids from get_outlets

tools.name: hub_update_modifier_choice
tools.title: Edit a choice
tools.description: Change one choice — its name, price, whether it is pre-selected, or where it is sold. Everything you leave out stays as it is. unavailableOutletIds is the exception list and REPLACES the stored one: pass [] to make the choice available everywhere again. Marking a choice unsold somewhere can be refused if a category requires more choices than would remain available at every outlet.

price.description: New extra charge, e.g. "0.90". Pass "0" to make it free

unavailableOutletIds.description: REPLACES the exception list. [] = sold at every outlet

tools.name: hub_update_outlet
tools.title: Update outlet
tools.description: Change the details of one outlet. Takes the outlet id from get_outlets, never a name. Only the fields you pass are changed; the rest are left alone. Renaming is safe and takes effect everywhere, including past orders and reports — they store the outlet id and look the name up. Country cannot be changed here: it belongs to the company. An alias that is already set cannot be changed either and the attempt is refused. Stripe account linking is not editable from here.

outletId.description: Outlet id from get_outlets — not a name

name.description: New outlet name

taxId.description: Business tax number printed on this outlet’s receipts (BN / GST / HST / VAT / EIN)

alias.description: Only settable while it is still empty

tools.name: hub_update_product
tools.title: Update product
tools.description: Change fields on an existing product. Takes the product ID — get it from get_products, never guess. Only the fields you pass are changed. Prices are HUMAN strings like "24.99". Variant fields (price, sku, barcode): for a product with several variants use `variants` with the ids from get_products; plain `price`/`sku`/`barcode` work only when there is exactly one variant.

productId.description: Product id from get_products — not a name

price.description: New price, only for a single-variant product

sku.description: New SKU, only for a single-variant product

barcode.description: New barcode, only for a single-variant product

variants.description: Per-variant changes; ids and labels come from the variants list in get_products

tools.name: hub_update_purchase_order
tools.title: Edit purchase order
tools.description: Rewrite an order that has not been sent yet. ONLY works while it is `suggested` or `draft` — a sent or received order is refused, because the supplier already has it. This REPLACES the whole order: the lines and charges you pass become the order, and anything you leave out is dropped. Read it with get_purchase_order first and send the full set back. This is also how a suggestion is ACCEPTED: editing a `suggested` order turns it into a `draft` and gives it its PO number. To accept one unchanged, pass its existing lines back verbatim.

supplierId.description: Supplier id — normally the order’s current supplier

outletId.description: Outlet id the goods will be received into

variantId.description: Item id from get_supplier_items — the supplier must carry it

quantity.description: How many, in the unit the item is sold in. May be fractional for goods sold by weight or length

unitCost.description: Cost per unit the merchant pays, e.g. "12.50". Never cents, never the selling price

discount.description: Flat discount on this line, e.g. "2.00". Not with discountPercent

discountPercent.description: Discount as a percentage of this line’s goods

feePerUnit.description: Extra cost per unit on this line

lines.description: The complete new set of lines

discount.description: Flat discount on the whole order, e.g. "25.00". Not with discountPercent

discountPercent.description: Discount as a percentage of the items subtotal

shippingFee.description: Shipping charged on the order, e.g. "18.00"

dutyFees.description: Duty / customs charged on the order

customFees.description: Any other named charge on the order, e.g. "Handling"

tools.name: hub_update_role
tools.title: Update role
tools.description: Change what a role allows, or rename it. This is the tool for "let cashiers give discounts" or "stop them seeing the reports" — it changes things for EVERY person on that role at once, so name them from get_roles when you confirm. PERMISSIONS ARE POWER. Confirm with the merchant first, naming the person and the role out loud ("give Maria the Manager role — yes?"), and never act on a role change you inferred rather than were asked for. The change is live on the next request: rights are re-read from the role every time, so no one logs out and no agent key stops working — including yours, if the change reaches your own account. Grant and revoke by permission id: grant ids from get_permissions, revoke ids from the role’s granted list in get_roles. Permissions you do not mention are left exactly as they are. You cannot edit the role you are signed in under — the cabinet locks it too, because it decides your own powers. Ask someone on another role. To move one person instead of changing the role, use assign_role.

name.description: New name for the role

tools.name: hub_update_supplier
tools.title: Update supplier
tools.description: Change one supplier’s details. Only the fields you pass change; the rest are left alone, and a blank string is ignored rather than blanking the stored value. Renaming is safe — past purchase orders store the id and look the name up. A name already used by another supplier of this company is refused. This does NOT change item costs: those live on the supplier–item link, so use link_supplier_items to re-price.

supplierId.description: Supplier id from get_suppliers — not a name

tools.name: hub_update_tax_group
tools.title: Update tax group
tools.description: Rename a tax group, make it the standard one, or change the ORDER its rates are charged in. Takes the tax group id from get_taxes, never a name. Order matters for money: a compounding rate is charged on the running total including everything above it, so reordering changes what customers pay. rateIdsInOrder must list exactly the rate ids already in the group, once each — it reorders, it never adds or removes. Use add_tax_rate_to_group / remove_tax_rate_from_group for that. CONFIRM WITH THE MERCHANT before reordering or changing the standard group. Sales already rung up are NOT recalculated — this only affects sales from now on.

taxGroupId.description: Tax group id from get_taxes — not a name

name.description: New name for the group

isStandard.description: Make this the company default group

rateIdsInOrder.description: Every rate id currently in the group, in the new charging order. A permutation, nothing else

tools.name: hub_update_tax_rate
tools.title: Update tax rate
tools.description: Change a tax rate’s name or its percentage. Takes the tax rate id from get_taxes, never a name. THE RATE IS SHARED: this changes EVERY tax group that lists it, not just the one the merchant was talking about. Call get_taxes first, tell them exactly which groups are affected, and get an explicit yes. If they only meant one group, the answer is a separate rate via create_tax_rate, not this tool. percentage sets the same value at every outlet. perOutlet REPLACES the stored per-outlet list whole — an outlet you leave out STOPS charging this rate, so read the current values back with get_taxes and resend every outlet that should keep charging. Sales already rung up are NOT recalculated — this only affects sales from now on. Reports and receipts for past sales keep the old rate.

taxRateId.description: Tax rate id from get_taxes — not a name

name.description: New name for the rate

percentage.description: New percentage at every outlet, e.g. 13 for 13%

perOutlet.description: Outlet-specific percentages, using outlet ids from get_taxes. REPLACES the stored list whole — an outlet you leave out stops charging this rate

percentage.description: Percent as the merchant says it: 13 means 13%. Not a fraction — 0.13 would mean 0.13%

tools.name: hub_update_user
tools.title: Update team member
tools.description: Change a team member's own details: name, phone, till PIN, and which outlets they work at. Takes the userId from get_team, never a name. Only the fields you pass change, but outletIds REPLACES their whole outlet list — read it back from get_team first and resend the ones that should stay, or you will quietly cut someone off from a location. Email cannot be changed here at all (the sign-in identity is not rotated, so the old address would keep working) — the merchant has to remove and re-invite the person. This tool does NOT change permissions: for that use assign_role.

userId.description: User id from get_team — not a name

outletIds.description: Replaces the outlets they may work at, ids from get_outlets. Omit to leave untouched

tools.name: hub_upload_media
tools.title: Upload images
tools.description: Store image files from public URLs in the media library so the merchant can use them later. Returns the stored URL of each file. JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF, up to 20MB each. This ONLY stores the files — it attaches them to nothing. If the merchant wants a photo ON A PRODUCT, use add_product_images instead: it uploads AND attaches in one step, and doing it here first would upload the same picture twice. Use this one when they just want the file kept — a logo, a banner, a picture for later. A file uploaded here may not appear on the cabinet's Media screen, which is fed by a separate service; the file is stored and its URL works regardless.

imageUrls.description: Public URLs of the images to store

tools.name: list_packs
tools.title: List packs
tools.description: Every tool pack with its product, description, tool count and whether it is allowed for this connection and listed right now.

tools.name: switch_company
tools.title: Switch company
tools.description: Choose the company Hub tools act on, by id or name (get_connection lists them). Remembered on this connection.
